title: CompletableFuture vs Future: blocking vs non-blocking, chaining, composition
keyPoints: Future (Java 5) provides only blocking get(), polling isDone(), and cancellation, with no callbacks or chaining.
CompletableFuture (Java 8) adds non-blocking callbacks, chaining, composition, error handling, and manual completion.
Future forces the caller to block or poll; CF lets you register callbacks that fire automatically when the result is ready.
CF provides allOf() and anyOf() for combining multiple futures, which Future cannot do.
CF supports manual completion with complete() and completeExceptionally() for testing and integration.
CF is a superset: it implements Future and adds the full async programming model.

s1_definition.oneliner: Future provides only blocking get() and polling isDone(), while CompletableFuture adds non-blocking callbacks, chaining with thenApply/thenCompose, composition with thenCombine/allOf/anyOf, error handling with exceptionally/handle, and manual completion.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Future<V>** (Java 5) – a handle to a pending result; limited to `get()` (blocking), `isDone()` (polling), and `cancel()` (cancellation).
- **CompletableFuture<V>** (Java 8) – a complete async programming model; implements Future and adds callbacks, chaining, composition, error recovery, and manual completion.
- **Blocking vs non-blocking** – Future forces you to block or poll; CF registers callbacks that fire automatically.
- **Chaining** – Future has none; CF has thenApply, thenCompose, thenAccept.
- **Composition** – Future cannot combine futures; CF has thenCombine, allOf, anyOf.
- **Manual completion** – Future cannot be completed from outside; CF has complete() and completeExceptionally().
s1_definition.analogy: Future is like submitting a form at National Bank of India and getting a token number. All you can do is wait at the counter until they call your number (blocking get()). You cannot say "when ready, call me." CompletableFuture is a smart pager. It vibrates when ready (callback). You can chain instructions: "when ready, calculate tax, then send receipt." You can combine: "when both balance and score are ready, decide the loan." You do not have to stand at the counter.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Future (Java 5)               CompletableFuture (Java 8)
  ┌──────────────────┐          ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │ get() (blocks)   │          │ thenApply (chain)         │
  │ isDone() (poll)  │          │ thenCompose (flatMap)     │
  │ cancel()         │          │ thenCombine (merge)       │
  │                  │          │ allOf / anyOf             │
  │ No callbacks     │          │ exceptionally (recover)   │
  │ No chaining      │          │ handle (transform)        │
  │ No composition   │          │ whenComplete (observe)    │
  │ No manual        │          │ complete() (manual)       │
  │ completion       │          │ orTimeout (Java 9)        │
  └──────────────────┘          └──────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Future (Java 5) is a simple handle to a pending result. It provides blocking get(), polling isDone(), and cancellation. Nothing else. No callbacks, no chaining, no composition, no error handling pipelines.

CompletableFuture (Java 8) is a complete async programming model. It adds non-blocking callbacks that fire automatically when the result is ready. It adds chaining with thenApply and thenCompose. It adds composition with thenCombine, allOf, and anyOf. It adds error handling with exceptionally, handle, and whenComplete. And it adds manual completion for testing and integration.

The biggest difference is blocking vs non-blocking. Future forces the caller to block or poll. CompletableFuture lets you register callbacks and free the calling thread. At National Bank of India, migrating from Future polling loops to CF callback chains reduced code by 60% and lowered latency by 40% through parallel composition.

Remember one sentence: Future blocks and polls, CompletableFuture chains and composes.
